nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $b \le c$ implies $a + b \le a + c$ and $b + a \le c + a$, and let $L$ and $R$ be lists over $\alpha$. Suppose that $l$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous run of $L$, $r$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous run of $R$, $s$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of $L$, and $p$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty prefix of $R$. Then…
nodes.title: Maximum subarray sum of a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $a \le b$ implies $a + c \le b + c$. Let $p$ be a list over $\alpha$, let $e$ be the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of $p$, and let $b$ be the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous sublist of $p$. Then for every $x \in \alpha$, the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous sublist of the list obtained by appending $x$ to $p$ is $\max(b, \max(x, e + x))$.
nodes.title: Maximum subarray sum after appending an element

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $a \le b$ implies $a + c \le b + c$. If $e$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of a list $p$ over $\alpha$, then for every $x \in \alpha$ the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of the list obtained by appending $x$ to $p$ is $\max(x, e + x)$.
nodes.title: Maximum suffix sum after appending an element

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $a \le b$ implies $a + c \le b + c$. If Kadane's algorithm returns a value $m$ on a list $L$ over $\alpha$, then some nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$ has sum $m$.
nodes.title: Kadane's algorithm returns an attained sum

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order. For a list $xs$ over $\alpha$ and $p \in \alpha$, $p$ is the maximum prefix sum of $xs$ when some nonempty prefix of $xs$ has sum $p$ and every nonempty prefix of $xs$ has sum at most $p$.
nodes.title: Maximum prefix sum

nodes.summary: For a list $L$ over an additive monoid $\alpha$ with a linear order, an element $m \in \alpha$ is the maximum subarray sum of $L$ when some nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$ has sum $m$ and every nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$ has sum at most $m$.
nodes.title: Being the maximum subarray sum

nodes.summary: For a list $L$ over an additive monoid $\alpha$ with a linear order, an element $e \in \alpha$ is the maximum suffix sum of $L$ when some nonempty suffix of $L$ has sum $e$ and every nonempty suffix of $L$ has sum at most $e$. A nonempty suffix is a contiguous run ending at the last element of $L$.
nodes.title: Being the maximum suffix sum

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $a \le b$ implies $a + c \le b + c$. Let $p$ be a list over $\alpha$, let $e$ be the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of $p$, and let $b$ be the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous sublist of $p$. Then for every list $r$ over $\alpha$, the value that Kadane's scan from the accumulators $e$ and $b$ returns on $r$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty…
nodes.title: Invariant of Kadane's scan

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order. For all accumulators $e, b \in \alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$ of length $n$, Kadane's scan of $L$ from the accumulators $e$ and $b$ costs exactly $3n$.
nodes.title: Cost of Kadane's scan

nodes.summary: Given accumulators $e, b$ in an additive monoid $\alpha$ with a linear order, the scan over the empty list returns $b$ at cost $0$. Over a list with first element $x$ and remaining elements $L$, it sets $e' = \max(x, e + x)$ and returns the result of the scan of $L$ from the accumulators $e'$ and $\max(b, e')$, at cost $3$ plus the cost of that scan.
nodes.title: Kadane's scan

nodes.summary: For lists over an additive monoid with a linear order: on the empty list it returns $0$ and on a one-element list $[x]$ it returns $x$, both at no cost. On a list of length $n \ge 2$, let $m = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, let $l$ and $r$ be its results on the first $m$ elements and on the remaining $n - m$ elements, let $s$ be the best nonempty suffix sum of the first $m$ elements as computed by the suffix scan, and let…
nodes.title: Divide-and-conquer core of maximum subarray

nodes.summary: The function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by $T(n) = 0$ for $n \le 1$ and $T(n) = T(\lfloor n/2 \rfloor) + T(n - \lfloor n/2 \rfloor) + 2n + 3$ for $n \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Cost recurrence of divide-and-conquer maximum subarray

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $b \le c$ implies $a + b \le a + c$ and $b + a \le c + a$. For every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the divide-and-conquer maximum subarray algorithm and Kadane's algorithm return the same result on $xs$.
nodes.title: Divide and conquer agrees with Kadane's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $b \le c$ implies $a + b \le a + c$ and $b + a \le c + a$. For every list $xs$ over $\alpha$ and every $m \in \alpha$, the divide-and-conquer algorithm returns $m$ on $xs$ if and only if $m$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous run of $xs$.
nodes.title: Correctness of divide-and-conquer maximum subarray

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order. On a nonempty list over $\alpha$ of length $n$, the cost $T$ of the divide-and-conquer maximum subarray algorithm satisfies $T + 3 \le 2n\lceil \log_2 n \rceil + 3n$, that is, $T \le 2n\lceil \log_2 n \rceil + 3(n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Running time of divide-and-conquer maximum subarray

nodes.summary: The CLRS algorithm FIND-MAXIMUM-SUBARRAY over an additive monoid with a linear order, returning only the sum. On the empty list it returns no value, at no cost. On a nonempty list it returns the value of the divide-and-conquer core on that list, at the same cost; the core splits a list of length $n \ge 2$ after its first $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ elements and returns the largest of its results on the two parts and the…
nodes.title: Divide-and-conquer maximum subarray

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order such that $a \le b$ implies $a + c \le b + c$. For every list $L$ over $\alpha$ and every $m \in \alpha$, Kadane's algorithm returns $m$ on $L$ if and only if $m$ is the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$: some nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$ has sum $m$, and every nonempty contiguous sublist of $L$ has sum at most $m$.
nodes.title: Correctness of Kadane's algorithm

nodes.summary: Over an additive monoid $\alpha$ with a linear order, Kadane's algorithm on a list of length $n \ge 1$ costs exactly $3(n - 1)$ operations, and on the empty list it costs $0$.
nodes.title: Cost of Kadane's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type with an additive monoid structure. On the empty list, Kadane's algorithm returns no value. On a list $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ of elements of $\alpha$ with $n \ge 1$, it sets $e = b = x_1$; then for $i = 2, \dots, n$ in turn it replaces $e$ by $\max(x_i, e + x_i)$ and then $b$ by $\max(b, e)$; finally it returns $b$. Each of the steps $i = 2, \dots, n$ is charged three…
nodes.title: Kadane's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order. If an element $m \in \alpha$ is the maximum subarray sum of a list $L$ over $\alpha$, then $L$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: A list with a maximum subarray sum is nonempty

nodes.summary: For lists over an additive monoid with a linear order, the prefix scan returns $0$ on the empty list at no cost, and $x$ on a one-element list $[x]$ at cost $2$. On a list with first element $x$ and nonempty tail $t$ it returns $\max(x, x + b)$, where $b$ is the prefix scan of $t$, at the cost of the scan of $t$ plus $2$.
nodes.title: Prefix scan

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid with a linear order. For every nonempty list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the suffix scan of $xs$ returns a pair whose first component is the sum of $xs$ and whose second component is the maximum sum of a nonempty suffix of $xs$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the suffix scan

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive monoid carrying a linear order. For a nonempty list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ in $\alpha$, this timed computation returns the pair $(x_1 + \dots + x_n, s)$, where $s$ is the maximum of the suffix sums $x_i + \dots + x_n$ over $1 \le i \le n$. It scans from the right: the step for $x_i$ forms $x_i + (x_{i+1} + \dots + x_n)$ and takes its maximum with the best suffix sum found so far, at a cost of…
nodes.title: Right-to-left suffix scan

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type with an additive monoid structure in which $b \le c$ implies $b + a \le c + a$. If Kadane's algorithm returns the value $m$ on a list $L$ over $\alpha$, then every nonempty contiguous run of $L$ has sum at most $m$.
nodes.title: Kadane's algorithm bounds every nonempty run

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type with an additive monoid structure, and let $L$ be a list over $\alpha$. If $m, m' \in \alpha$ are both maximum subarray sums of $L$, meaning that each is the sum of some nonempty contiguous run of $L$ and bounds the sum of every nonempty contiguous run of $L$, then $m = m'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the maximum subarray sum

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
